p8.text: Progress 8 is not published for independent schools.

notes.since: Change is measured from 2022/23, the first year graded on the normal scale.
notes.middleHalf: The band is the middle half of 10 nearest with results that year (the 25th to the 75th percentile). Schools without results are left out.
notes.rollIndexed: Each line is indexed to 100 in 2019/20. The set's lines are the average roll of 10 nearest: day pupils across its 10 schools with a census in every year shown and 2 with boarders for the boarding line, so a school opening or closing doesn't move them.
notes.trendYears: Each trend covers the years its measure has. Results are measured from 2022/23: 2021/22 was graded more generously. Sixth-form value added starts in 2023/24: DfE published none for the two years before, because those students' GCSEs were teacher-assessed. Progress 8 stops at 2023/24: there were no Key Stage 2 tests in 2020 or 2021, so later pupils have no baseline. Rolls run from the 2019/20 census.

notes.points: Points per entry, with DfE's grade equivalent. Each line is ranked within its own qualification only, among the schools in its comparison set with a figure: A-level points never sit beside BTEC points. Top-grade shares are in the views.
notes.vaPost16: Value added compares each student's results with others nationally who started from similar GCSEs. 0 is England's average; the range is DfE's 95% confidence interval, and a range that crosses 0 isn't clearly different from average. Small cohorts have wide ranges.
notes.bandsDfe: Bands: DfE's own progress band where DfE publishes one (A level, Academic, Applied general, Tech level). Elsewhere VicData's three, from the 95% range alone: Clearly above (the whole range above 0), In line (it crosses 0), Clearly below (the whole range below 0), deliberately unlike DfE's five.
notes.bandsP8: Progress 8 bands are derived exactly from DfE's definition: the figure and its 95% range (well above or below beyond ±0.5 with the range clear of 0).
notes.p8Gap: Progress 8 stops at 2023/24: there were no Key Stage 2 tests in 2020 or 2021, so later pupils have no starting point.
notes.vaGap: DfE published no sixth-form value added for 2021/22 or 2022/23: those students' GCSEs were teacher-assessed.
notes.applied: Applied general and Tech level are DfE's two headline types. DfE sorts qualifications into them by subject, so one school's BTECs and OCRs can fall in both. The individual qualifications and sizes are in the subject-areas view.
notes.epqNoPoints: VicData doesn't hold EPQ points yet, so the EPQ has entries and value added but no points figure.
notes.tlevelNoVa: DfE publishes no value added for T levels: attainment only.
notes.quarters: Coloured by quarter within the set (top quarter, middle half, bottom quarter); the line marks the set's median.
notes.subjectsByQual: Each subject is ranked only against the same subject in the same qualification, among the set's schools that teach it.
notes.vicdataMatch: † placed in its subject area by VicData: DfE's value-added file names the subject differently from its results file (VicData's list, approved by Guy, in the shared subject crosswalk).
notes.outsideAreas: The EPQ sits outside the subject areas.
notes.size: XS to XL: the subject's entries against every school in England entering that subject in that qualification that year (fifths).
notes.sizePending: The XS to XL sizes against England arrive once their table is loaded.
notes.mix: Entries, not students: each qualification group's share of the year's Post-16 entries (VicData's groups).
notes.setMoves: The set's schools: the biggest three rises, then the biggest three falls, last year to this.
notes.lines: Last year to this, every line in column 1, each on its own scale.
notes.setHolds: A set you choose holds across the qualifications: each view shows its schools that offer the chosen one.
notes.smallEntries: Subjects with fewer than 5 entries aren't ranked: one or two pupils would decide the rank.
notes.middleHalf: The band is the middle half of 10 nearest offering A level with results that year (the 25th to the 75th percentile). Schools without results are left out.
notes.eachLine: Each line is ranked in its own qualification's comparison set: the 10 nearest schools offering it.
notes.entries: Entries, not students: each group's entries and its share of all the school's Post-16 entries, against the set's typical school (the median of the set's schools offering it).
notes.share: Share = the subject's entries as a share of all the school's Post-16 entries; the set's typical share is the median of the set's schools offering it.
notes.moves: The biggest changes in entries since 2022/23.
notes.against: Share of the school's Post-16 entries, against the set's typical school offering the subject.

notes.aroundSchool: Around the school: every school within 15 km, all sectors.
notes.children: Pupils aged 11–18 in schools within 15 km (school census): children who go to school nearby, wherever they live. Children living within 15 km (ONS estimates) are not pupils at schools within 15 km (census): two different counts, and neither is divided by the other.
notes.births: Births are counted by local authority (ONS), by calendar year.
notes.projection: A projection of children living in the area, not a forecast for the school: children aged 11–18 living within 15 km, aged forward a year at a time from those already counted, at the area's own record of families moving in and out.
notes.popByAge: Residents by single year of age living within 15 km (ONS estimates, mid-2024): where children live, not where they go to school.
notes.shade: Shading by district: until the neighbourhood boundaries are loaded, the map shades whole local authorities by the pupils of these ages in their schools (school census).
notes.nearby: Children aged 11–18 living within 15 km, against Reading and England (ONS mid-year estimates), indexed to 100 in 2012.
notes.population: Children aged 11–18 living within 15 km: estimates to mid-2025, then the projection to 2036, its band shaded.
notes.sources: ONS mid-year population estimates for LSOAs (mid-2024) and local authorities (mid-2025); the children-in-an-area projection (settings version 2), and ONS's 2022-based subnational projections for births' change and the comparison line; ONS births by local authority; DfE school census (pupils at schools nearby); English Indices of Deprivation 2025 (MHCLG); DfE “Schools, pupils and their characteristics” (2025/26).
